issues.where: He in whom brilliance shines is strong
issues.problem: yasya tejaḥ virājate is genitive ('whose brilliance shines'); 'in whom' turns it into a locative and changes the case sense (Hindi जिसका is right).
issues.fix: He whose brilliance shines is strong

patch.old: He in whom brilliance shines is strong
patch.new: He whose brilliance shines is strong

issues.problem: Glossary fixes virājate = shines (शोभा देता है).
Locative absolute agrees with dīpe (m.); gender missing.
vajramātram is neuter singular beside masculine plural nagāḥ; not mentioned.

patch.text: vajramātraṃ is neuter singular beside masculine plural nagāḥ; read as a predicate 'only the size of a thunderbolt', as in the parallel hastimātraḥ and dīpamātram.

issues.problem: 'addicted' is stronger than straiṇa (the draft's own note says 'given to women'); not in the Sanskrit.

The genitives gṛhāsaktasya, māṃsabhojinaḥ, dravyalubdhasya, straiṇasya are rendered with 'for', a preposition the Sanskrit lacks; glossary asks to keep genitive case sense (of one attached to the home, no learning). Needs a human choice of Hindi wording (e.g. की/का), so no patch.
issues.fix: Of one attached to the home, no learning; of a flesh-eater, no compassion; of one greedy for riches, no truth; of one given to women, no purity.

issues.problem: Labelled 'dvandva' for three members, but the ending is dual (the notes admit the mismatch); the label asserts a grouping the form does not support.
'With' is added; the Sanskrit has a bare accusative plural. Even though disclosed in the notes, it is an added word that fixes the relation.
'से' added (same problem); keep the bare accusative.
Note becomes stale after the two fixes.

patch.old: 'with' is supplied in translation as the evident relation to the śrāddha (it could also be read as the offering performed).
patch.new: it is left bare in the translation; its relation to the śrāddha (means or offering) is not stated in the Sanskrit.

issues.problem: Glossary: karma = action. 'work' departs from the fixed rendering.
issues.fix: he whose action is trade and agriculture

patch.old: he who has trade and agriculture as his work
patch.new: he whose action is trade and agriculture

issues.fix: having trade and agriculture as action

patch.value: having trade and agriculture as action

issues.problem: Glossary: dāra = wife (पत्नी), strī = woman; para-dāra is 'another's wife'. English already says wife.
'gen. pl.' omits that it is the first-person pronoun.
English 'of Bali, of the lord of valour' reads vikramapateḥ as apposition to Bali. After 'baleḥ ca' it may equally be a third person; the notes mention name/epithet but not this.

patch.text: The comma before 'of the lord of valour' follows the Sanskrit order only; vikramapateḥ after baleś ca could be a third person rather than an epithet of Bali.

issues.problem: The suggestion rests on sense, but nāśam 'destruction' as object of saṃcitam is no clearer than nātham. A neuter participle agreeing with rahitaṃ and saṃcitaṃ (e.g. naṣṭaṃ 'lost') suits 'long-hoarded, devoid of giving and enjoying of honey' better on sense and shape. Flag only; no source in hand, so mark as a guess. Needs a human edit of the flag.
issues.fix: suggest: naṣṭaṃ (possible, from sense and agreement only)

summary: 17 issues: 3 error, 14 minor. Main errors: u3 'in whom' for yasya (genitive); u11 added 'With'/'से' on a bare accusative. No regrouping suggested. Units 1,2,4,6,7,8,9,12,14,15,16 ok. Confidence labels honest (u18 low, flagged forms kept as printed).
